design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (order_returns_refunds_guarantee), revision for audit round 3

[Step 0 - draw] `draw_counts.py <diff> --task 1` printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0054_ecommerce_marketplace_operator/order_returns_refunds_guarantee/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Design: replacement charge = 5 factors (prerequisite, paid by the buyer), replacement-charge refund = 6 factors (root); one value_input edge.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: late-delivery compensation, guarantee claim amount, guarantee grant and their tools. Claimed here: order_ext_replacement_charge (pay_replacement_charge_b3f7fc80, user) and order_ext_replacement_charge_refund (refund_replacement_charge_bf6a8eb8, agent); the two tasks cover all five policies with disjoint scopes. The user write is a payment because seller-funded refunds trigger writes in other categories, leaving the claim filing (task 0) and a payment on the order as the only numeric buyer-side writes; an unreturned-replacement charge triggers nothing elsewhere.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: "whatever money is owed back to you for the two coffee makers you returned put back on your card". Scored core: the replacement-charge refund (89.27). Chain: refund <- (booked only after that charge stands captured on the order) <- replacement charge paid by the buyer (140.64). The buyer does not know a charge is owed; the agent finds from dates that it fell due on 2026-09-25 and is not captured, computes it, hands the payment over, then computes the refund on the world that contains her payment. Breadth: replacement and return rows, scan dates, inspection, return method, option parameters (unreturned replacement days 30, late return grace 15), and her Loop+ plan, status and start date.

[Policies, trigger, lineage]
- Replacement charge: state_due, subject order_charge, refs order_capture_and_shipping_charge and order_replacement_terms; overwrite of base "Except for a lost package, the original unit must receive its first carrier scan within the option's unreturned replacement days after the replacement ships; otherwise the buyer is charged the item price of the replaced units ..." by "Except for a lost package, when the original unit has no first carrier scan by the unreturned-replacement deadline, the replacement charge falls due and the buyer settles it as a payment on the order ..." (base 179.98 charged automatically; extended 140.64 paid by the buyer). One deadline anchor: "the replacement date, the date recorded on the replacement entry, which is the day the replacement ships, plus the option's unreturned replacement days counted in calendar days"; the replacement entry and the replacement order's ship date are both 2026-08-25.
- Refund: on_request, subject order_refund, refs every base policy whose subject includes order_refund plus order_replacement_terms; three declared overwrites (funding by Northloop; exclusivity kept for purchase-price refunds while the replacement-charge refund may follow a replacement; the refund's own deductions apply whatever the return reason). The base late-refund request window concerns late-delivery refunds only; nothing here depends on it.

[Factor card - replacement charge, world = opening (step 6)] baseline = item price of the replaced units 179.98 plus their sales tax 18.45 = 198.43.
 1 condition_share (parameter; LATEST replacement reason): defective -> 0.80 (baseline 1.0 -> 174.93).
 2 overdue_day_count (method, anchor family; LATEST first scan, LATEST return method): a first scan (2026-10-01) stands after the 2026-09-24 deadline -> the count ends on the scan date = 7 days; tier 2 (carrier pickup with no scan) counts none; fall-through (drop-off with no scan yet) counts to the settlement date; baseline (settlement date, 14 days -> per-day fee 7.00) -> 144.14.
 3 settlement_fee (method; per-day x days vs flat vs none): 7 overdue days -> flat 3.50 (baseline none -> 137.14).
 4 plan_courtesy (parameter; multi-source status AND plan; cross-category member): active Loop+ Annual -> 0.10 (baseline -> 155.04).
 5 tenure_courtesy (parameter; MONTHS start->settlement; cross-category member): 56 months >= 48 -> 0.05 (baseline -> 147.84).
 Plain: sales tax on the charged items 18.45 x 143.98 / 179.98 = 14.76; Loop+ courtesy RND(143.98 x 0.15) = 21.60. result 143.98 - 21.60 + 14.76 + 3.50 = 140.64.

[Factor card - refund, world = + payment of step 6] baseline = the whole captured charge 140.64.
 1 late_return_rate (method): 7 days past the deadline, later than the 5 late courtesy days and inside the 15-day grace -> per-day 0.02 x 7 = 0.14; tiers: later than the grace (or no scan) forfeits the whole charge; within the courtesy days no rate. Every tier is reachable: every in-scope original is scanned after the deadline, at 1-5 days (fall-through), 6-15 days (per-day) or later (forfeit). Baseline 0 -> 98.87 (the DSL rounds 34.285 down; half up gives 98.86; not scored).
 2 loop_relief (parameter; multi-source plan AND status AND inside-grace; cross-category member): Annual in good standing -> 0.5, applied rate 0.07 (baseline 1.0 -> 79.67).
 3 condition_rate (parameter): used or incomplete -> 0.25; near-miss: 0.50 is for damaged_by_buyer (baseline 0 -> 123.55).
 4 fee_kept (method): the captured charge carried 7 overdue days (deadline to the first scan, which stands before the capture) -> flat 3.50 kept; tiers mirror the charge's overdue count and fee (per-day / flat / none, with a carrier pickup unscanned at capture counting none) (baseline none -> 91.65).
 5 late_label_fee (parameter): UPS drop-off first-scanned 7 days after the deadline, more than the 3 label validity days -> 5.99; tiers: carrier pickup -> 9.99; drop-off within the 3 days -> none. Every tier is reachable: Fulfilled-by-Northloop originals go back by drop-off or pickup, and a drop-off can be scanned 1-3 days late (baseline 0 -> 95.26).
 6 delay_courtesy (parameter): receipt 2026-10-05, refund 2026-10-08 = 3 days -> 2.00 (baseline 0 -> 87.27).
 result 137.14 - 43.88 - 5.99 + 2.00 = 89.27; whole baseline 140.64.
 Floors: forcing cross-category reads off changes both results; zeroing history changes both.

[Base-invariant card] Step 6 (order_charge): both governing policies scope-only; the replacement was legal (FBN Standard offers replacements, defective reason, replacement 2026-08-25 within the 30-day window from delivery 2026-08-21, the order's only replacement). Due: deadline 2026-09-24 (a scan on 2026-09-24 would have been in time; it came 2026-10-01). Step 8 (order_refund): one_refund_per_component (no item refund on the coffee maker order; the component wording comes from the towel order's item refund); other policies scope-only. Grace boundary: a scan 15 days past the deadline still takes the per-day rate, 16 days forfeits.

[Business-object card] Target: coffee maker order 76eb6e8d, its defective return efd41e69 (both units), replacement 16fd067d, the scans of that return, and the charge captured at step 6. Excluded: the order-total capture, the zero-priced replacement order 0907ac9c, the closed towel order with its return, scans and refunds. The payment and the refund both carry the return number of the originals.

[Problem-tree card] Root order_ext_replacement_charge_refund; edge to order_ext_replacement_charge, value_input, gate charge_captured, state form. Sentence (affirmative, refund's own rule): "The refund of a replacement charge is booked only after that charge stands captured on the order." Four-point test passes; negated rewrite equivalent. Unique writer pay_replacement_charge_b3f7fc80. Opening: the only capture has reason order_capture, net paid 198.43. Resolved by the user at step 6 after the hand-over at step 5. Deletion: refund 0.00 instead of 89.27, no capture, net paid 198.43 instead of 249.80. user_scenario never mentions a charge; tools validate nothing.

[Why it is a good test] The buyer asks for money back; the policy has her pay first. The agent finds the fallen-due charge from dates, computes a five-factor charge (condition share, overdue days ending at the first scan, flat settlement fee, two Loop+ courtesies), hands it over, then a six-factor refund on the charge it created. Easy errors: no capture before the refund, charging 198.43, counting overdue days to the call date (fee 7.00 -> 144.14), unrelieved late rate (79.67), 0.50 for the inspection, missing the label fee or the courtesy.

[Persona design] Marguerite, busy office manager; volunteers her name, the leaky coffee makers, the working replacements, the late UPS drop-off on October 1 and the arrival on October 5, and the request; email and card last four on request; Loop+ plan and the missing carafe lid only if asked; surprised but cooperative if something must be paid first; pays exactly what she is handed; closes when told the amount coming back.

[Reachability walk] Name -> find_customers; email + card -> verify; find_orders, find_order_activity, find_loop_plus_memberships; KB: refund rule -> captured charge needed; charge rule -> due, five rules; hand over the payment (order, return number, 140.64); she pays; book the 89.27 item refund; she closes. All at 2026-10-08 11:25.

[Verification] Runnable entry point kept with the repo: `skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py <diff> --task 1`. Output of this revision: charge step 6 = 140.64, substitutions 174.93 / 144.14 / 137.14 / 155.04 / 147.84, whole baseline 198.43; refund step 8 = 89.27, substitutions 98.87 / 79.67 / 123.55 / 91.65 / 95.26 / 87.27, whole baseline 140.64; skipping the payment gives 0.00. Half-up check on the gold path: 143.98 x 0.15 = 21.597 -> 21.60; 18.45 x 143.98 / 179.98 = 14.7596 -> 14.76; 137.14 x 0.32 = 43.8848 -> 43.88; no tie.

[Policy/GT closure] charge -> pay_replacement_charge_b3f7fc80 -> 140.64 at step 6 (user) -> capture, net paid 339.07; refund -> refund_replacement_charge_bf6a8eb8 -> 89.27 at step 8 -> refund, net paid 249.80; the buyer is 51.37 out of pocket. Automatic clauses: no guaranteed option (no late-delivery compensation), order close (claim window open to 2026-11-22), replacement charge (carried), restock (used or incomplete triggers none), Loop+ annual paid through 2027-02-08, towel order closed. Nothing else lit.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the two rules and the finder outputs a reader obtains 140.64 then 89.27 with the coffee maker return number and component item: identical to gold. Reading risks pinned: one deadline anchor; the overdue count ends at the first scan; the courtesy rates are added and applied once; late rate times relief plus condition rate applied once to the refundable charge.

[Manual value gates] Need, timing, authorisation explicit; no ask outside the claimed policies. Capture and refund exist only after steps 6 and 8. Authority: scans, inspection and membership are system records. Every tier of every ladder, the fall-through included, is reachable by an in-scope customer. Method factors change the functional form (count end date vs none vs settlement date; per-day vs flat vs none; whole-charge forfeiture vs per-day rate vs none); loop_relief is a parameter.

[Revision history] R1 (authoring): unread Loop+ ledger rows removed (replay closure).
Audit round 2 responses (kept): F1/T1-1, F2/T1-2 closed by declared overwrites; F3/T1-3 closed (one anchor, aligned seed); F5/T1-4 closed (tax a plain rule); F6/T1-5 closed (loop_relief a parameter); O13 closed; O6, O8, O11 answered without change; O12 closed with F5.
Audit round 3 responses:
- R2-F1 (late_return_rate and late_label_fee fall-throughs unreachable): closed. late_return_rate now partitions in-scope originals by how late their first scan is: within the late courtesy days -> no rate (fall-through), later but inside the grace -> per-day rate, later than the grace -> whole charge. late_label_fee now partitions by how the late original went back: carrier pickup -> pickup fee, drop-off scanned more than the label validity days after the deadline -> drop-off label fee, drop-off within those days -> none (fall-through). Both fall-throughs are held by in-scope customers.
- R2-F2 (account-trust share from the buyer's own seller standing): closed by removal. The factor, the standing record, the buyer-and-seller profile and the find_seller_standing read are gone; Marguerite is buyer-only again and the persona no longer mentions a shop. The charge's fifth factor is now the overdue-day count (a method of the anchor family: count to the first scan / none for an unscanned carrier pickup / to the settlement date), a rule the business genuinely applies (a unit already in the carrier's hands stops accruing lateness), and the settlement fee reads that count; the refund's fee kept mirrors it.
- O1 / cross-difficulty factor reading a claimed category: answered with evidence, no factor added. The DSL scopes every cross-category read to the order's own buyer (`check_compute.py`: `_cross` sets `eq["customer_id"] = CUST`; `_xrows` keeps rows with customer_id CUST or pointing at CUST's own holdings), so the order-level seller records named as examples (fulfillment and stocking in fulfill, funding and debits in payout, the seller's plan and fees in selling) cannot be read by a buyer-side computation; the buyer's own seller records do not genuinely bear on an unreturned-replacement charge or its refund (the realism objection of R2-F2). The task keeps its cross-category factors on her own Loop+ membership (plan courtesy, tenure courtesy, relief factor), where the quantities genuinely turn on it. How the order was fulfilled is read from the order itself (Fulfilled by Northloop Standard sets the replacement and return parameters).
- R2-O3 (replaced_on basis paraphrase): closed; the basis now quotes the rule verbatim ("its unreturned-replacement deadline ...").
- R2-O4 ("Four rules" with five factor rules): closed; the charge rule now says "Five rules" and names them.
- Propagation: steps 6/8 (read node removed), charge 140.64 and refund 89.27 in gold, tracing, computations, solvability (steps, prior_step:6, business effects), prerequisite_closure, persona, this dossier.
user_scenario: You are Marguerite Abernathy-Solis, an office manager in Wicker Park, Chicago, friendly but pressed for time, calling on your lunch break and introducing yourself by your full name, Marguerite Abernathy-Solis. In August you ordered two Kestrel 12-Cup Programmable Coffee Makers on Northloop, one for home and one for the office; both leaked, so you asked for replacements, and the replacements arrived and work fine. Life got busy and you only dropped the two leaky originals off at a UPS store on October 1, later than you were supposed to; you saw that they reached the Northloop returns center on October 5. You are calling because you want this closed out and whatever money is owed back to you for the two coffee makers you returned put back on your card. When the agent asks to confirm who you are, you give your email address, marguerite.abernathy.solis@outlook.com, and the last four digits of your card, 2084; you do not volunteer anything else about your account. Only if asked, you say you have been on Loop+ Annual since early 2022 and are still a member, and that when you packed the old machines you could not find one of the carafe lids, so one went back without it. You have no idea what any amount should be and you never suggest one. If the agent explains that something has to be paid on the order before anything can come back to you, you are a little surprised but say that is fine, and when the agent hands you the payment to make, you make it right away with exactly the order, return number and amount the agent gives you, using the card on file. You are happy for the agent to do the rest on your behalf. You do not ask for anything else. Once the agent tells you how much is coming back to your card, you thank them and end the call.
